gbm_population_evidence.quote: Patients with high-grade glioma (HGG) who have recurred/progressed after receiving standard treatment and confirmed to meet the 2021 edition of the World Health Organization (WHO) classification criteria for central nervous system tumors by histopathology

candidate_evidence.quote: Inject Ad-TD-nsIL12 into the tumor via Ommaya reservoir, administering on days 1, 4, and 7, and infuse a PD-1 inhibitor on day 9.
evaluating the preliminary efficacy and safety of the oncolytic virus Ad-TD-nsIL12 in combination with a PD-1 inhibitor for the treatment of recurrent HGG

candidate_flag.reason: Only pharmacological candidate is an unnamed PD-1 inhibitor given with the oncolytic virus; not a separately registered intervention.

role_evidence.quote: A Study on the Novel Oncolytic Virus Combined With PD-1 Inhibitor in the Treatment of Recurrent High-grade Glioma

agents.drug_class_hint: oncolytic adenovirus expressing non-secreted IL-12 (Ad-TD-nsIL12, BioTTT001), intratumoral via Ommaya
arms: Evaluation of the efficacy of the novel oncolytic virus Ad-TD-nsIL12 combined with PD-1 inhibitors

role_evidence.quote: On the 7th day (±3 days) after oncolytic virus administration each cycle, a PD-1 inhibitor is given, or until disease progression or the occurrence of intolerable toxicity.

agents.drug_class_hint: anti-PD-1 checkpoint antibody, agent not named in record

flag.reason: PD-1 inhibitor is unnamed and not a registered intervention; listed because every patient receives it per protocol text.

arms: Evaluation of the efficacy of the novel oncolytic virus Ad-TD-nsIL12 combined with PD-1 inhibitors

coder_notes: Population is recurrent high-grade glioma per WHO 2021 with no explicit mention of glioblastoma anywhere -> high_grade_glioma_unspecified (excluded at S5). Oncolytic virus is an excluded intervention type; the PD-1 inhibitor (unnamed) is the only pharmacological agent, coded experimental_monotherapy by analogy with manual example (checkpoint inhibitor + vaccine).
